fix.summary: Touch tables and rows in the same order everywhere: Make every code path that changes shop.customers and shop.orders do it in one order (for example, always the parent row first, and rows sorted by key). Then the second transaction waits instead of deadlocking.

findings.summary: Two transactions locked shop.customers and shop.orders in opposite order and waited on each other; session 202's transaction was rolled back. Each transaction had already changed rows the other one wanted next: session 202 was running “UPDATE shop.customers SET name = name WHERE id = 1” and session 201 “UPDATE shop.orders SET status = status WHERE id = 1”. With the same order in both, the second would simply wait instead of deadlocking.
findings.title: Two queries deadlocked once in the last day (opposite access order on shop.customers and shop.orders)
verify: Re-scan tomorrow: no new opposite access order deadlocks on shop.customers and shop.orders.
